ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the characters of the name; hop 4 acts on the gold's boolean (an impermissible name gives IllegalArgumentException, otherwise the Option is constructed) and hops 1-3 only set properties on the Option they get back. Once the gold answers false for the one-character name '?', no caller can recover an Option under that name, and no caller can pre-filter it, because an Option's name cannot be changed after construction. The convention is pinned outside the gold: OptionValidator.validateOption, which every Option constructor applies (also on the Options.addOption path), documents and implements the permissible names: null, a single Java identifier part or '?' or '@', and longer names of Java identifier parts only (isValidOpt: isValidChar(c) || c == '?' || c == '@'); the facade's javadoc defers to Option for what a valid name is. Passing tests pin the rest of the rule through the chain: testIllegalOptions (the names '"' and 'opt`' rejected, 'opt' accepted), testBuilderIsResettedAlways (a rejected name, then the builder is reset), OptionsTest.testHelpOptions (the null names of long-only options and the digit names '1' and '2' accepted). Edits above the gold that pass the suite all discard or override the gold's answer: hop 4 consulting the gold only for longer names or not at all (the constructor's validator then decides), hop 4 accepting '?' and '@' itself, or a hop constructing the Option directly.
